notabeneDefinitions.warning: Current legal GBP 800 branch and vendor EUR 1000 artifacts are independent; do not infer vendor selection from law.

vendorTriggeredAdditional.mismatch: Vendor definition permits legal-person national identification and does not constrain natural-person national ID to the three statutory document types.

jurisdictions.lawNotes: Current law changed from EUR 1000 to GBP 800 on 2026-06-30. If all executing cryptoasset businesses carry on business in the UK, paragraph 6 information is supplied on beneficiary-business request rather than automatically by threshold. Law permits account number or, if absent, unique transaction identifier.
jurisdictions.simulatorDisclaimer: Scenario aid only; do not infer compliance or normalize unique identifiers without an explicit mapping.

vendorAdditional.mismatch: FR-0 four-way pick is broader than Article 14(1)(d); a single address, document number, or customer ID is legally insufficient for the first branch.

jurisdictions.lawNotes: EUR 1000 is not a general EU Travel Rule threshold. It is an exceeds boundary for self-hosted ownership/control assessment.
jurisdictions.simulatorDisclaimer: Evaluate Article 14 and FR-0 independently. Passing FR-0 does not establish that Article 14(1)(d) is satisfied.

jurisdictions.lawNotes: The CFR rule is broader than the five IVMS field groups in US-3000.
jurisdictions.simulatorDisclaimer: Below-threshold behavior is UNKNOWN; do not return no requirements merely because US-0 is absent.

notabeneDefinitions.boundaryConflictWarning: Do not select SG-1500 at equality solely from its filename.

jurisdictions.legalPersonMismatch: PSN02 permits date and place of incorporation or registration as appropriate. SG-1500 has an empty legal-person path array for the date-and-place descriptor.
jurisdictions.lawNotes: PSN02 says below or equal for paragraph 13.4 and exceeding for paragraph 13.6.
jurisdictions.simulatorDisclaimer: Use decimal > 1500 for the enhanced legal branch; retain vendor-selector status as UNKNOWN.

jurisdictions.unknownReason: Collected FSA English evidence establishes a 2023-06-01 effective date and broad scope but not an exhaustive 2026 field/equality/covered-jurisdiction rule. Absence is not proof.
jurisdictions.simulatorDisclaimer: Label output Notabene implementation view; do not present it as complete Japanese law.

secondaryLegalAssessment.claim: Vendor narrative and audit secondary corroboration support no de minimis and address OR customer ID; primary Japanese law not fetched, so exact scope is not closed.

jurisdictions.unknownReason: Published FA pseudo-jurisdiction and FA-1000 artifact are VERIFIED. Universal runtime fallback, comparator, precedence, below-threshold behavior and determination that local law is absent remain UNKNOWN.
jurisdictions.simulatorDisclaimer: Require explicit customer opt-in/configuration and display UNKNOWN comparator; never silently substitute this for legal advice.

jurisdictions.disclaimer: Assumed rates are intentionally illustrative and are not evidence of market price or a compliance conclusion.

questions.question: What are the supported production regions, data-residency boundaries, failover topology, and feature-parity matrix for V2 and Flow? Nearest evidence: [V2 OpenAPI](https://node-open-api-specs.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/openapi.json).

What uptime, latency, recovery-time, recovery-point, maintenance, and support-response commitments are contractually available? Nearest evidence: [Getting Started](https://devx.notabene.id/reference/getting-started-with-your-api).

Which Transact V1 surfaces and the Node SDK are planned for deprecation, what is the supported V1-to-V2 migration sequence, and what is the production compatibility matrix across V2, Flow, SafeConnect, TAIPs, and `tap-ts` versions? Nearest evidence: [NodeJS SDK](https://gitlab.com/notabene/open-source/notabene-nodejs).

Which license authoritatively governs TAP (the repository’s CC0-1.0 or README’s CC BY-SA 4.0), who owns its IP/trademarks and appoints maintainers, and which of `tap-ts`, `tap-rs`, `tap-go`, or TAIPs `schemas/` and `test-vectors/` is normative for conformance? No distinct “TAP Parser” was found in the enumerated public sources; private/historical existence is not disproven. Nearest evidence: [TAIPs repository](https://github.com/TransactionAuthorizationProtocol/TAIPs).

For the documented Flow payout operations, what is the complete `flowState` transition enum, webhook catalog, retry/reversal behavior, regional availability, and launch status? Nearest evidence: [raw V2 OpenAPI](https://node-open-api-specs.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/openapi.json).

What are the exact recurring-payment mandate, consent, cancellation, renewal, retry, and revocation APIs? Nearest evidence: [Flow end-to-end examples](https://devx.notabene.id/docs/end-to-end-examples.md).

What actor, delegation credential, signer, spending limit, consent, revocation, and liability model applies to announced agentic payments? Nearest evidence: [Ripple announcement](https://notabene.id/post/notabene-announces-strategic-investment-from-ripple).

What transitions and operational meanings apply to transfer `AWAITING-YOURS` / `AWAITING-COUNTERPARTY` and agent `REPLACED` / `UNREACHABLE`? Are any terminal, recoverable or replaced by callbacks? Which is accepted at runtime: policy enum `REQUIRE_AUTHORIZATION` or the schema example `RequireAuthorization`? Nearest evidence: [Statuses explained](https://devx.notabene.id/docs/statuses-explained), [V2 schema](https://node-open-api-specs.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/openapi.json).

What are the transaction-isolation, concurrency, idempotency, and conflict semantics across transfers, agents, relationships, policies, and repeated settlement IDs? Nearest evidence: [V2 OpenAPI](https://node-open-api-specs.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/openapi.json).
What ordering, duplicate window, maximum delay, replay window, retention, and delivery guarantees apply to Svix webhooks? Nearest evidence: [Webhook flow](https://devx.notabene.id/docs/webhook-flow).

The V2 SDK transformer accepts `delegateToken`; which deployed hosted-component flows use it, and what TTL, claims, endpoint scopes, audience, CORS policy, revocation and browser-placement rules apply? Do not reuse the V1 five-minute TTL by assumption. Nearest evidence: [SDK](https://gitlab.com/notabene/open-source/javascript-sdk), [V1 customer token](https://devx.notabene.id/docs/customertoken.md).

What are the delegate JWT’s TTL, complete claim set, permission matrix, revocation mechanism, rotation behavior, and safe placement? Nearest evidence: [Create delegate token](https://devx.notabene.id/reference/createdelegatetoken.md).

How are organizations, users, entities, environments, and OAuth clients bound in RBAC, and how are client secrets rotated or emergency-revoked? Nearest evidence: [Authentication](https://devx.notabene.id/reference/authentication-2.md).

How is control of a `did:web` domain proven, monitored, and recovered after DNS/HTTPS or registrar compromise, and what overlap exists during key rotation? Nearest evidence: [DIDdocs explained](https://devx.notabene.id/docs/diddocs-explained.md).

Who can access Node signing and key-agreement private keys in each hosting model, and are keys HSM/KMS-backed, exportable, backed up, tenant-isolated, rotated, and securely destroyed? Nearest evidence: [Key Management in DIDdocs](https://devx.notabene.id/docs/key-management-in-diddocs.md).

In managed PII mode, which services or operators can access plaintext, and what are the field-level retention, backup, legal-hold, deletion, residency, and audit policies? Nearest evidence: [Encryption managed by Notabene](https://devx.notabene.id/docs/encryption-by-notabene).

In customer-managed mode, which outer-envelope metadata and nested ciphertext are visible, logged, transiently processed, or retained; which Flow/V2 paths support it; and how are recipient-key rotation and undecryptable messages handled? Nearest evidence: [Customer-managed encryption](https://devx.notabene.id/docs/self-encryption.md).

Which current production paths use P-256 `#pii`, X25519, legacy Ed25519-to-X25519 PII SDK encryption, or escrow/hybrid mode; which DIDComm profile protects each message class; and what is the migration plan between them? Nearest evidence: [go-didcomm](https://github.com/Notabene-id/go-didcomm).

How does production choose a presentation definition when originator/beneficiary jurisdictions conflict, direction differs, a counterparty requests more data, or entity configuration is stricter? Nearest evidence: [PII requirements](https://devx.notabene.id/docs/pii-requirements.md).

Which exchange-rate source, valuation instant, precision, rounding, stale-rate, and linked-transfer aggregation rules select threshold branches? Nearest evidence: [Jurisdiction threshold index](https://pd.notabene.id/ivms101/v2/jurisdiction-thresholds.json).

When will the GB selector/definitions reflect regulation 64C’s **GBP 800, `>=`** rule substituted by **SI 2026/621 regulation 32**, effective 30 June 2026, what FX/linked-transfer logic is used until then, and how are customers notified of rule-version changes? Instrument identification is resolved; vendor implementation timing is not. Nearest evidence: [current regulation 64C, annotation F2](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2017/692/regulation/64C).

How does Notabene reconcile `FR-0`’s four-way one-of with Article 14(1)(d)’s compound **(address + document + customer ID) OR (date + place of birth)**, and where are DLT addresses and conditional LEIs carried? Nearest evidence: [EU Regulation 2023/1113](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1113).

Which pay-in `settlement_address` contract is deployed—the quickstart’s asset-only body or OpenAPI’s required address—and what are confirmation-depth, reorg, duplicate-hash, failed-fiat, reversal, fee, and reconciliation semantics for subsequent settlement? Nearest evidence: [PRA pay-in quickstart](https://devx.notabene.id/docs/quickstart-pra-respond-to-pay-ins.md) and [raw V2 OpenAPI](https://node-open-api-specs.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/openapi.json).

What exact API, event, key-custody, liability, and version boundaries apply to DFNS, Ripple Custody, RLUSD, Ripple Payments, and Flow IP participation? Nearest evidence: [common use cases](https://devx.notabene.id/docs/common-usecases.md).

What pricing meters, rate limits, fair-use limits, audit/export rights, subprocessor commitments, breach obligations, indemnities, insurance, termination assistance, and data-portability guarantees apply? Nearest evidence: [Notabene developer documentation](https://devx.notabene.id/llms.txt).

Who confirms the on-chain payment that moves a micro-transfer proof out of `pending`, with what confirmation depth, timeout, reorg and error contract? Public documentation assigns screenshot review, not this duty. Nearest evidence: [wallet verification](https://devx.notabene.id/docs/self-hosted-wallet-verification-1.md).

When will `XX_old` be retired, duplicates BR/LI_old/IS_old removed, and customers notified? Which of US-3000, US1-3000, US2-0 and US0-0 is authoritative for each product? What do ID/GI near-1,000 strings mean at equality? Nearest evidence: [threshold index](https://pd.notabene.id/ivms101/v2/jurisdiction-thresholds.json).

Can Notabene supply auditable source for shipped `cli`, `reactnative-sdk`, `ops` and `verify-proof`, clarify unavailable repository URLs and document support/EOL despite absent npm deprecation flags? Nearest evidence: [registry search](https://registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/search?text=notabene&size=50).

What is the purpose/support status of `@notabene/appkit`, whose scope/publisher attribution differs from its Reown repository/author metadata? Nearest evidence: [package metadata](https://registry.npmjs.org/@notabene%2fappkit).
